title: Love for your brother
hook: none of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself
tomorrow: a hard hadith about life and death. what's its heart?

segments.voice: Yesterday: leave what doesn't concern you, but goodwill always concerns you. Not my concern. Today, the goodwill gets a measure.

Two friends apply for the same internship. One gets it. The other types congrats, with three exclamation points, and means about half of it. Yesterday's question asked what you wish for the person standing next to you. Anas ibn Malik reports the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, setting the bar exactly there. None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
screen: `CONGRATS!!! (HALF MEANT.)` → `WHAT DO YOU WISH FOR THEM?` → `AS FOR YOURSELF.`

segments.voice: Not until he loves his brother, which is easy enough on a good day. Loves for him: wants for him the same good he wants for himself. The internship, the health, the good name, the guidance. And the hadith ties it to faith itself. So who counts as a brother? In one narration in Sahih Muslim, the wording is: for his neighbor, or he said, for his brother. Some commentators read brother as a fellow believer; others widen it to every person. The Qur'an widens the frame on its own, in Pickthall's words: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another." One human family, many tribes, made to meet. Here's ground Muslims share with a neighbor. The Torah says it in Leviticus, in the JPS 1917 translation: "thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself." And a story in the Talmud has the sage Hillel sum up the Torah for a man in a hurry: what is hateful to you, don't do to your fellow; the rest is commentary, go and learn. The same bar, in Jewish words: yourself as the measure. And one honest difference. In Leviticus it comes as a commandment, sealed with I am the LORD. In the hadith it comes as a measure of faith: none of you believes until. One is an order to keep; the other is a mirror to check.
screen: `NOT LOVES HIM: LOVES FOR HIM.` · `NEIGHBOR, OR BROTHER.` · `NATIONS AND TRIBES, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.` · `AS THYSELF: LEVITICUS AND HILLEL.` · then, large: `AS FOR MYSELF.`

segments.voice: Count three good things you have right now on your fingers: maybe health, a friend, an hour of quiet. For each one, let a face come to mind, someone who could use the same, and wish it for them as fully as you'd want it yourself. If someone difficult comes to mind, wish it for them too.
screen: `THREE GOOD THINGS.` · `A FACE FOR EACH.` · `AS FULLY AS FOR YOURSELF.`

segments.voice: Love for your brother: wanting for someone else the good you want for yourself. The hadith makes it a measure of faith.
To hold on to: as for myself, the same good I want, wished for the next person too. Fifteen days in.

howItsDone: Muslims quote this hadith when teaching manners, envy and friendship, as a test for checking one's own heart; some teachers pair it with Qur'an 49:13 on nations and tribes.

fork.setup: your teammate gets the starting spot you wanted. after the game she's down about a mistake she made. what fits today's hadith?
options: help her get better, the way you'd want someone to help you.
stay polite, but let her figure it out; it's her spot now.
point out the mistake to the coach, since honesty matters most.
fork.reveal: loving for her what you love for yourself means wanting her good, even in the spot you wanted. that's the hadith's measure of faith.

chat.says: jordan's helping at our class bake sale. a kid asked if jordan counts as a 'brother' since not muslim
options: One narration says neighbor. Either way, wish Jordan the good you want for yourself.
No. Brother only means Muslims here, so the hadith doesn't cover Jordan.
Yes, because every religion is basically the same, so we're all one faith.
chat.meaning: Commentators differ on 'brother', one narration says 'neighbor', and the Qur'an calls all people nations and tribes made to know one another.

Anas ibn Malik.meaning: a companion who served the Prophet and reported this hadith

Sahih Muslim.meaning: a major collection of hadith, gathered by Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj

Torah.meaning: the five books of Moses, Jewish scripture's first part

Hillel.meaning: a Jewish sage whose sayings are kept in the Talmud

Talmud.meaning: the rabbis' collection of Jewish law and discussion
